To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

African American/Black patients’ perceived provider’s cultural sensitivity, perceived provider’s impartiality (fairiness), and perceived trust of provider are significant predictors of their satisfaction with provider care.

perceived provider cultural sensitivity and perceived provider fairness (impartiality) are significant predictors of patients’ satisfaction with their provider and that some of the predictive relationships between perceived provider cultural sensitivity, and patients’ satisfaction with provider care, were partially mediated by patients’ perceived provider fairness (perceived provider impartiality) and trust of the provider.

African American/Black patients’ perceptions of their provider’s cultural sensitivity, including their perceptions of their provider as impartial, are important in patients’ reported satisfaction of their provider.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how patients perceive the cultural sensitivity of their providers, and how this perceived cultural sensitivity influences their satisfaction with their providers’ care.
the roles of perceived provider cultural sensitivity, perceived health care justice (impartiality and trust), and patient satisfaction with care in patient-provider interactions.
the development of a patient-centered culturally sensitive health care model (PC-CSHC model) and its components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three dimensions and the overall perceived provider cultural sensitivity are important in patients’ satisfaction with their provider care and that patients’ trust of and perceived provider impartiality are important mediators of this linkage.

the present study provides evidence for the first refined component of the PC-CHSC Model, which links perceived provider cultural competence and perceived provider health care justice to patients’ satisfaction with provider care.
the present study provides evidence for the refined first component of PC-CSHC Model and that the refined first component is a valid and reliable model for future studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present findings support the refined first component of our PC-CSHC Model and provide a basis for the development of the second component of the model.
the PC-CSHC model has been developed, tested, and is being used as a framework for the development of culturally sensitive interventions.

the three dimensions (i.e., cultural knowledge, cultural humility, and cultural competence) of provider cultural sensitivity, as perceived by the patients, are significant predictors of the patients’ satisfaction with their provider and that these predictive relationships are mediated, in part, by the patients’ perceived provider justice and their trust of their provider.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the three dimensions (i.e., cultural awareness, cultural competence, and cultural humility) of perceived provider cultural sensitivity are important for patients’ satisfaction with provider care, and that perceived provider impartiality and trust of provider are key mediators of this linkage.
the PC-CSHC model is a promising model that can guide future work on patient-centered care.

the PC-CSHC model is a useful framework for understanding how patients perceive and experience their provider-patient interactions, and how patients’ perceptions and experiences influence their health care outcomes.
